label: Endorsed by the practice's own standards: P.OwnStandard m: the practice's own authoritative…
term: endorsed by the practice's own standards
definition: `P.OwnStandard m`: the practice's own authoritative standards endorse m as a correct move, as opposed to a standard imported from outside the practice (a philosopher's, a scientist's).
note: Analytical vocabulary (#1010). Which instances count as the practice's own standards is not fixed here; for the Catholic practice the open bridge STMT-CONCILIAR-DEFINITION-IS-PRACTICE-OWN-STANDARD counts conciliar definitions among them.

formal_gap.meaning: Practice.OwnStandard m says that the practice's own authoritative standards endorse the move m as correct, as opposed to a standard imported from outside the practice (a philosopher's or a scientist's). It is a field of a religious practice viewed as a language game (TruthCore.Alternatives.Fideism, #1010), supplied by each model.
examples: A conciliar definition of the Catholic practice, under the open bridge STMT-CONCILIAR-DEFINITION-IS-PRACTICE-OWN-STANDARD.
exclusions: Endorsement by a standard from outside the practice.
Merely theological formulation or a practical role in religious life: DISAMB-THEOLOGICAL-FORMULATION-AND-NORMATIVE-GRAMMAR separates these from normative own-standard endorsement.
open_obligations: Which instances count as the practice's own standards is not fixed; STMT-CONCILIAR-DEFINITION-IS-PRACTICE-OWN-STANDARD, STMT-AUTHORITY-GRAMMAR-MAKES-DEFINITIONS-OWN-STANDARD and STMT-USE-GRAMMAR-MAKES-ORDINARY-USE-OWN-STANDARD are open bridges into it.
STMT-WF-RELIGION-INTERNAL-GRAMMAR (own-standard moves are correct) is an open fideist commitment.
No formalization candidate from existing vocabulary.
